title: 🚀 2. Mini-Bar & Quick Settings
content:
2. Mini-Bar & Quick Settings

2.1 UI Elements & Controls (Mini-Bar)

The Mini-Bar is an ultra-compact floating toolbar engineered to occupy minimal screen space while providing full execution control. Controls from left to right:

  • ● (Status Dot): Indicates target virtual environment health.
    • Green: Environment is valid, healthy, and located on disk.
    • Red: Environment is missing, corrupted, or path is broken.
  • INFO Text / Group Selector: Displays active Project and Venv (in Single Mode), or Container Group (in Multi Mode).

  • ▶ Play: Executes assigned script or runs container group.
  • ■ Stop: Instantly terminates the running script or entire process group.
  • ⚙ (Gear Icon): Toggles the flyout Quick Settings panel.
  • 🖥 (Monitor Icon): Opens the full Master Manager window.
  • 📌 (Pin Icon): Toggles 'Always on Top' mode above IDEs and other windows.
  • M (Mode): Toggles between Single (single project) and Multi (container orchestrator) modes.
  • ✕ (Close): Completely exits VenvHub Pro.

2.2 Quick Settings (Flyout Panel)

Clicking the ⚙ gear icon expands the Quick Settings flyout panel, allowing instant parameter adjustments without launching the main Manager.

Available Quick Controls:

  1. Project & Venv: Fast switching between workspace projects and linked virtual environments.
  2. Target Script: Shows target entry point script configured in the Master Manager.
  3. Language & Skin Theme: Real-time interface language and QSS skin switcher.
  4. Express Package Install (Pip/UV): Enter package name (e.g. requests) and hit Install. Directly installs into the active Venv using default package manager.

2.3 Temporary Override vs. Permanent Venv Assignment

A core architectural feature of VenvHub Pro: clear separation between Quick Settings adjustments and Master Manager assignments.

Temporary Override (RAM Only) - Quick Settings

Changing the active Venv in Quick Settings applies strictly in-memory (RAM).

  • Ideal for rapid experimentation and testing in alternate runtimes.
  • Leaves project configuration JSON untouched.
  • Reverts to default assigned Venv upon application restart.

Permanent Assignment (Default) - Master Manager

To permanently assign a Venv to a project, open Master Manager (🖥) and check the 'Default' checkbox in the project matrix.

Tip: Default permanent Venvs are highlighted with a star (★) inside the Quick Settings dropdown list.

2.4 Execution Modes

Under 'Actions', you can configure the behavior of the Play ▶ button:

  • Open Terminal: Opens an activated CMD terminal at project root without executing script. Useful for manual CLI tasks.
  • Run in Terminal (Default): Spawns a dedicated console window, activates Venv, and runs the script with live stdout/stderr stream.
  • Run in Background (Silent): Runs process invisibly without window creation. Designed for GUI applications and background services.
Silent Mode Notice: Because no console window is created, terminate background processes via the Stop ■ button on the Mini-Bar or via Task Manager.

2.5 Multi-run Mode on Mini-Bar

Clicking the M button switches the Mini-Bar into container orchestration mode:

  • The single project label transforms into a Group Dropdown Selector.
  • The ⚙ Quick Settings button is hidden (settings apply at container level).
  • Play ▶ and Stop ■ buttons control the entire process group simultaneously with hooks and respawn watchdogs.
Productivity: Start and stop your entire microservice stack (Frontend, Backend, DB) directly from your desktop toolbar with a single click.
